final_words:
I played for about three minutes. I'd keep playing for a while longer, though I doubt it would hold me for very long.

**What I think the game is:** a cozy idle/incremental game set in a moonlit tailor's workshop. You turn a big brass gear by clicking it, or faster by holding it down, to earn "spirals" of winding energy. The pale shapes on the floor are sheets with sleeping clockwork dolls under them. A thread runs from the gear to a ring over one of the sheets, and when the ring fills, the spirals are spent, that doll wakes up and the workshop gets a new item.

**What I understood:**
- Clicking adds 1 spiral; holding adds about 3 per second at first.
- My first doll (top hat) woke at about 33 spirals, and a desk lamp came on. After that, spirals also came in on their own.
- Each new doll added a gear to the big one and went off to help wind the next sleeping doll. A red sewing machine appeared along the way, so income kept speeding up.
- By the end I had 3 dolls awake, 4 small gears, a lamp and the sewing machine, and the three dolls were working on a fourth sheet, its ring about half full.

**What confused me:**
- A tutorial hand appeared after I'd already worked out the clicking. Seeing it, I wondered whether there was a hidden action I was missing.
- Clicking the glowing face-button near the shelf, the floor sheets or a full-looking ring did nothing. I couldn't tell whether the button has a purpose.
- The rings don't show how much they cost. I thought the second ring was full and clicked it, but it still had a small gap.
- I never tried the two icons at the top left or the restart button at the top right.

**Would I keep playing?** For a little while. Waking each doll and watching the room fill up and glow brighter is charming, and it shows progress well. But the only real input is holding down one gear, and I didn't see any choices to make. I'd keep going to see what the mannequin, the grandfather clock and the floating button do, but unless real decisions show up, I'd expect to lose interest once those are revealed.
